title: Bushels Held Back in Store Against Unpaid Storage Charges
content:
Bushels are held back against what the account owes the elevator, since grain is not released against unpaid charges. This rule governs releases out of store under Grain Storage and Conditioning Agreements.

## Clause

Where conditioning charges and storage accruals both stand unpaid on the account, the wide charge holdback of 1500 bushels stays in store.

Where exactly one of conditioning charges and storage accruals stands unpaid on the account, the light charge holdback of 600 bushels stays in store.

And otherwise, nothing standing unpaid on the account at all, nothing is held back for charges.

## Where each line bites

| Conditioning charges standing unpaid | Storage accruals standing unpaid | Held back in store |
| --- | --- | --- |
| some | some | 1500 |
| some | none | 600 |
| none | some | 600 |
| none | none | nothing |

What is read is whether money of each class stands unpaid at all, not how much of it there is.

## Worked holdbacks, on hypothetical accounts

**An account carrying an unpaid conditioning charge of 240.00 and an unpaid storage accrual of 88.50.** Both classes stand unpaid, so 1500 bushels stay in store.

**An account carrying an unpaid storage accrual of 88.50 and no conditioning charge outstanding.** Exactly one class stands unpaid, so 600 bushels stay in store.

**An account on which every charge has been settled.** Nothing is held back for charges.
